importErrors.invalid_url: The repository URL is not valid. Expected: https://host/group/project.
importErrors.credentials_in_url: Remove the credentials from the URL: use the “Access token” field.
importErrors.host_not_allowed: This host is not allowed. Add it to GIT_HOSTS (Cairn's allowlist of Git hosts).
importErrors.unauthorized: Token refused, expired or missing the required permissions.
importErrors.not_found: Repository not found, or the token has no access to it.
importErrors.branch_not_found: This branch does not exist in the repository.
importErrors.rate_limited: Provider rate limit reached. Try again later.
importErrors.unreachable: Host unreachable from Cairn (network, proxy or certificate).
importErrors.timeout: The provider did not answer in time.
importErrors.git_missing: git is not installed on the machine running the worker.
importErrors.secret_key_missing: CAIRN_SECRET_KEY is not configured (token encryption key).
importErrors.interrupted: Import interrupted (worker stopped). Start it again.
importErrors.internal: Internal error. See the worker logs.
importErrors.forbidden: Action reserved for the super administrator.
importErrors.queue_unavailable: The job queue is unavailable. Try again.
importErrors.import_conflict: An import is already running for this repository and branch.
importErrors.rescan_conflict: A scan is already running for this repository.
importErrors.exists: A project with this name already exists in this team.

form.step1Hint: Cairn really queries the provider to check the token, the repository and its branches.
form.token: Access token (optional for a public repository)
form.tokenHint: Read-only is enough: GitLab read_api + read_repository, GitHub “Contents: Read”. The token is encrypted (AES-256-GCM) before storage and never shown again.
form.listTruncated: List truncated: enter the exact name, it will be checked on import.
form.checkedOnImport: This branch will be checked on import.
form.teamHint: Required · created if it does not exist yet.
form.importHint: The worker clones only this branch (history truncated to the last commit), analyses the technical stack, then deletes the working copy.

page.title: Import a repository
page.description: Real clone of one branch from GitLab or GitHub, then analysis of the technical stack.
page.lockedDemo: The demo role (cookie) cannot authorise a real import in production. Configure OIDC authentication.
page.dbMissingBody: Set DATABASE_URL and CAIRN_SECRET_KEY, apply the migrations (pnpm db:migrate) and start the worker (pnpm dev:worker).
page.dbDownBody: Check that PostgreSQL is running (docker compose -f infra/docker-compose.yml up -d) and that DATABASE_URL is correct.

run.tokenNotShown: The token is not shown again: enter it again to retry.
run.branchMoved: The branch moved between the request and the clone: the analysed commit is the reference.
run.doneNote: Working copy deleted. Only the facts (technologies, number of files) are kept; no file content is kept.

scan.largestHint: The most expensive to read in full.
scan.secretsHint: Only the location and the key name are kept. The value is neither stored nor shown, and must not stay in the repository.
scan.runIncremental: Incremental scan since {previous}: {reused, number} unchanged files reused, {analysed, number} read again, {removed, number} removed.

scan.runFinished: Finished in {seconds} s on {date}. No AI involved: everything is read from the code.

page.title: CI/CD — {name}
page.summary: {provider} · {stages, plural, one {# stage} other {# stages}} · {environments, plural, one {# environment} other {# environments}} · from commit to {env}: {machine} of machine time · extracted on {date}

page.none: No CI/CD chain has been extracted for this project yet.
page.ciHint: Shared by every environment. What fails here never reaches a server.
page.risks: What the chain does not protect
page.risksHint: Inferred from the configuration itself. Each finding names the file to open to prove it wrong.
page.noRisk: None of the known rules fires on this chain. That does not mean it is safe: only that we have nothing to hold against it.
page.emptyHint: It is read from pipeline files and deployment manifests, not from a table maintained by hand.

imported.imagesHint: What the pipeline builds and publishes. The link opens the service in the architecture.
imported.variablesHint: The names the pipeline reads. Their values are never read nor kept by Cairn.
imported.environmentsHint: Configuration folders named after an environment. This is not the list of what is deployed.
imported.configFiles: {count, plural, one {# configuration file} other {# configuration files}}
imported.title: CI/CD — {name}
imported.description: From commit to production, read from the repository's pipeline.
imported.unavailableBody: The CI/CD chain appears after the first successful scan.
imported.noPipelineBody: No GitLab CI file, GitHub Actions workflow or Jenkinsfile was found in this repository. If the scan predates this view, run it again from the project sheet.
imported.nonBlocking: {count, plural, =0 {No job that stops nothing} one {# job that stops nothing} other {# jobs that stop nothing}}
imported.topologyHint: From commit to what runs: the tools, their logos and what they hand to each other. Solid line: written in the repository. Dotted: inferred, or not described.
imported.topologyOutdated: This scan predates the deployment diagram. Run it again from the project sheet to draw it.
imported.jobsDetailHint: The stages in pipeline order. Click a job to see when it runs, what it produces and what weakens it.
imported.findingsHint: Findings you can check in the file, with the line. Cairn proposes, it never changes the repository.
imported.noFinding: No point of attention found in the pipeline.
imported.limits: Everything comes from the pipeline file, read without running it. Durations, approvals, incident recovery and run history are not in it: Cairn does not invent them. Pattern-based reading, not a full YAML analysis: a job generated by an include or a dynamic rule may not appear.

board.noApproval: No approval — the chain carries on by itself

page.title: Getting started — {name}
page.summary: {handsOn} at the keyboard · up to {days, plural, one {# working day} other {# working days}} waiting for access · maintained by {maintainer} · checked on {date}
page.none: No setup procedure has been described for this project yet.
page.askToday: Ask for these today, before anything else
page.askTodayHint: The commands below take {handsOn}. These accesses take up to {days, plural, one {# working day} other {# working days}}, and nothing runs without them. Slowest first.
page.workstationHint: The versions are the ones the repository requires, not the latest released.
page.installHint: Each step says what success looks like, and the file it comes from.
page.pitfallsHint: The failures newcomers actually hit, described by what shows on screen rather than by their cause — it is the error message you will be looking at.
page.firstContributionHint: Deliberately small, local topics: the goal is to go all the way round — branch, fix, test, get it reviewed — not to deliver a lot.
page.wrongStep: A wrong or missing step? It is a defect of the repository, not of this page: tell {maintainer}.
page.emptyHint: An invented setup would waste more time than it would save.

imported.title: Getting started — {name}
imported.descriptionReadme: Local setup for a new developer, read from <mono>{path}</mono> and the build files.
imported.description: Local setup for a new developer.
imported.unavailableBody: The getting-started guide appears after a successful scan. If the scan predates this view, run it again from the project sheet.
imported.toolsHint: {count, plural, =0 {None required by the repository} one {# required by the repository} other {# required by the repository}}
imported.beforeYouStart: Good to know before you start
imported.beforeYouStartHint: The warnings the authors themselves wrote in the README.
imported.workstationHint: Versions taken from the pipeline and the build files when possible, otherwise from the README.
imported.installHint: The README commands, in the order it gives them, grouped by moment. Values that look like credentials are masked.
imported.noCommand: The README contains no command to run.
imported.toObtainSectionHint: Variables the pipeline expects and the repository does not provide. Only the names are read.
imported.localPathsHint: Paths written for an author's machine.
imported.urlsHint: What the README says to open once it runs.
imported.findingsHint: What slows a newcomer down, with the line it comes from.
imported.noFinding: The README covers the essentials of getting started.
imported.limits: Read from the README and the build files, never executed: Cairn does not know whether a command works today. Durations and accesses to request are not in a repository, so they are not shown.

docs.title: Documentation — {name}
docs.description: What is written, what is missing, and what no longer matches the code.
docs.unavailableBody: The documentation view appears after a successful scan. If the scan predates this view, run it again from the project sheet.
docs.driftHint: The documentation states one thing, the repository shows another. Each finding quotes the line.
docs.noDrift: No contradiction detected between the documentation and the repository.
docs.coverageHint: The questions a newcomer asks, and whether the documentation answers them.
docs.filesHint: The documentation files, with what it costs to read them.
docs.aiHint: The instruction files assistants read on their own. Cairn proposes them, it never writes them.
docs.limits: Pattern-based reading: Cairn compares quoted versions and paths, it does not judge the quality of the writing. A document can be accurate and missing from this list, or the other way round. Reading costs are estimates (size / 4).
